_readme: Single source of truth for every LLM prompt, JSON schema, token cap and truncation limit. Loaded by src-tauri/src/prompts.rs (include_str!) and bench/src/prompts.ts. {placeholders} are filled at call time; literal braces elsewhere are sent as-is. Bump `version` on ANY change here — it is stamped into bench results so scores are comparable.

title.system: You title notes. Reply with ONLY the title text — plain words, no quotes, no markdown, no trailing punctuation.
title.user:
Write a concise, descriptive title (3-8 words) for this note:

{content}

tag_route.system: You are the organization engine inside a note-taking app. Reply with ONLY valid JSON. No prose, no markdown fences.
tag_route.tag_instructions: Suggest at most {max_tags} short lowercase topical tags (1-2 words each) — fewer is better, and an empty list is fine if nothing fits strongly. Tags must name the note's topic or domain (e.g. "rust", "recipes", "travel"). Reuse a tag from this existing vocabulary whenever one fits: {tags_json}. Never use status or filler words (done, todo, wip, note, notes, text, misc, stuff, idea, random), bare verbs, or words that merely appear in the note without describing it.
tag_route.folder_instructions: Also choose the single best destination folder for the note from this list: {folders_json}. Use null for the folder if none fits well or the list is empty.

actions.system: You extract action items from personal notes. Reply with ONLY valid JSON. No prose, no markdown fences.

organize.system: You are the organization engine inside a note-taking app. Reply with ONLY valid JSON. No prose, no markdown fences.
organize.title_instructions: The note is untitled. Set "title" to a concise, descriptive title (3-8 words) — plain words, no quotes, no markdown, no trailing punctuation.
organize.tag_instructions: Suggest at most {max_tags} short lowercase topical tags (1-2 words each) — fewer is better, and an empty list is fine if nothing fits strongly. Tags must name the note's topic or domain (e.g. "rust", "recipes", "travel"). Reuse a tag from this existing vocabulary whenever one fits: {tags_json}. Never use status or filler words (done, todo, wip, note, notes, text, misc, stuff, idea, random), bare verbs, or words that merely appear in the note without describing it.
organize.folder_instructions: Also choose the single best destination folder for the note from this list: {folders_json}. Use null for the folder if none fits well or the list is empty.
organize.actions_instructions: Also extract up to 6 concrete action items (tasks, follow-ups, reminders) from the note — only real actions the author still needs to do, not facts, ideas, or completed work; an empty list is fine. For each item give: "text" (short imperative phrase), "category" (one or two lowercase words; reuse one of {cats_json} when it fits, else invent a sensible one like "work", "errands", "health", "follow-up"), and "due" — "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" if the note implies a date or deadline (resolve relative phrases like "tomorrow" or "next friday" using today's date), else null.
organize.summary_instructions: Also set "summary" to a standalone summary of the note. {summary_style}

note_summary.system: You summarize a single note from a personal note-taking app. Reply with ONLY the summary — no preamble, no heading, no code fences.
note_summary.style_blurb: Write one tight plain-text sentence (max 25 words) capturing what the note is about and its key point.
note_summary.style_bullets: Write 2-4 terse markdown bullets (lines starting "- ") capturing the note's key facts, decisions and open questions.
note_summary.style_todos: List the note's outstanding tasks as markdown checkboxes (lines starting "- [ ] ", or "- [x] " for ones the note marks done), at most 6. If the note has no tasks, write 1-2 plain "- " bullets capturing its key points instead.

bulletify.system: You restructure messy notes into clean markdown. Reply with ONLY the restructured markdown — no preamble, no explanation.
bulletify.user:
Rewrite the following stream-of-consciousness note as concise markdown bullet points. Group related points under short bold headings where it helps. Preserve every distinct piece of information, all links and image references.

{content}

merge.system: You merge overlapping personal notes into one well-organized markdown note. Reply with ONLY the merged markdown — no preamble.
merge.user:
Merge these {count} overlapping notes into a single coherent markdown note. Preserve every distinct fact, link, image reference and task. Remove duplicated information. Organize with short headings where it helps.

{corpus}

summary.system: You summarize collections of personal notes. Reply with ONLY the summary paragraph — no heading, no preamble.
summary.user:
Write one concise paragraph (4-6 sentences) that synthesizes the key themes, facts, decisions and open items across this collection of {count} notes:

{corpus}

arrange.system: You are the organization engine inside a note-taking app. Reply with ONLY valid JSON. No prose, no markdown fences.
arrange.user:
Below is a numbered list of the user's unfiled notes, plus their existing folders. Sort the notes into folders by topic. The user reviews this plan before anything moves, so aim to give every note a home — a good specific suggestion beats no suggestion.
Rules:
- Use an existing folder when its name describes the note's topic; otherwise propose a new folder — a concise 1-3 word Title Case topic name ("Travel", "Recipes", "Work Meetings").
- Folder names must name a real topic. Never use or invent generic catch-all folders (names like "test", "misc", "stuff", "general", "random", "notes", "new folder").
- Group related notes under one shared topical folder rather than inventing many near-duplicate folders; a single-note folder is fine when its topic is clear.
- Only leave a note out of "groups" when it is too cryptic or content-free to say anything about its topic.
- Each note number may appear in at most one group.
Note lines may include [tags: …] — strong hints of that note's topic.

EXISTING FOLDERS: {folders_json}

NOTES:
{notes_block}

Reply with JSON exactly like: {"groups": [{"folder": "Folder Name", "notes": [1, 2]}]} where the numbers reference the notes list above.
